articles.title: Vizio ramps up creator-led programming in bid for CTV ad dollars
articles.summary: Vizio, Walmart's connected TV platform, rolled out a major expansion of creator and premium content to attract advertisers, adding more than 40 creator-led channels to its free ad-supported service WatchFree+, featuring names like MrBeast, Amaury Guichon, Ryan Trahan, Rebecca Zamolo and "Hot Ones" from First We Feast, covering genres from gaming to food to travel. Guichon will also star in an exclusive series, "Holiday Chocolate Workshop." Vizio expanded programming partnerships with MGM, NBCUniversal, Disney, A&E and A24, bringing titles like "The Good Doctor" and "Law & Order" to a library now exceeding 45,000 movies and shows and 400 live channels. A WatchFree+ exclusive film, "Jingle Bells Wedding Bells," starring Rachel Bilson and Scott Foley, launches with Geico as presenting sponsor. Separately, Walmart Connect announced a Warner Bros. Discovery partnership bringing live TV inventory to its DSP for the first time, alongside a similar Spotify deal and expanded Yahoo DSP integration for Vizio via Magnite. Vizio OS reached 32 million active devices in H1 2026, up 20% YoY, while WatchFree+ viewing hours rose 58% in fiscal Q2 2027.
articles.li_summary: Walmart's Vizio launched 40+ creator-led channels on WatchFree+ featuring MrBeast and Amaury Guichon, plus new NBCUniversal, Disney and A24 content deals, as CTV ad spend is projected to hit $29.3 billion in 2026.

articles.title: Snapchat publishes 2026 holiday marketing guide
articles.summary: Snapchat has published an 8-page holiday marketing guide titled "Wrapped in the Chat" aimed at helping brands plan their 2026 holiday campaigns. The guide centers on the idea that holiday shopping now depends heavily on real-time, peer-to-peer validation within close social circles, with users discovering items, sharing them with trusted friends or family, gathering consensus, and then converting from consideration to purchase. It includes data points illustrating this behavior pattern, along with insights into specific times when Snapchat users are most actively searching for gift ideas and recommendations. The guide also walks marketers through how to effectively use Snapchat's different advertising formats to reach shoppers during this period, and it provides a planning checklist to help brands structure their holiday campaign strategy. With peer recommendations increasingly influencing purchase decisions, Snapchat is positioning itself as a key platform for connecting brands with shoppers seeking validated, socially-endorsed gift options throughout the holiday season.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat released an 8-page “Wrapped in the Chat” holiday marketing guide detailing 2026 shopping trends, peer-driven purchase behavior, gift-recommendation timing, and ad format tips for brands.

articles.title: Meta acquires multiple VR patents from Sony
articles.summary: Sony has transferred 43 U.S. patents covering AR and VR technology to Meta, according to Road to VR via ZDNet Korea, under a Confirmatory Assignment agreement signed in December 2025 that will eventually move 419 patents globally. The patents span XR-specific information processing, head-mounted display designs, and various smart glasses formats filed by Sony between 2010 and 2022, suggesting the company is stepping back from AR/VR hardware development entirely. Meta gains significant intellectual property and engineering insight that could strengthen its own headset and glasses roadmap. The move comes as Meta itself has been deprioritizing VR in favor of artificial intelligence, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg stating at last month's Meta Connect that superintelligence will arrive before the metaverse and prove more transformative. Still, Meta unveiled next-generation VR glasses at the same event, claiming they weigh five times less than the current Quest 3 headset, showing VR remains part of its longer-term plans. The Sony patent haul could help Meta combine AI and VR capabilities to solidify its position as the dominant player in the emerging spatial computing market.
articles.li_summary: Meta acquired 43 U.S. AR/VR patents from Sony in December 2025, with 419 global patents set to transfer overall, signaling Sony's retreat from headset development as Meta absorbs its XR technology.

articles.title: Meta launches advanced Muse Wonder AI models
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out its next-generation agentic AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, building on its existing Muse system with greater processing power for complex, longer-duration tasks that can take multiple days to complete. The new models combine Active Memory and Active Focus features to track user priorities and work toward specific goals, and Meta says they've achieved new high scores on key AI benchmark tests. The models apply specialized knowledge to real-world problems in law, finance, and health, such as interpreting a lease or financial documents, which Meta is using as evaluation criteria. However, this expanded capability raises data privacy concerns given Meta's history with data handling issues, plus safety risks already surfacing: a Toronto Muse user recently let his AI agent fully manage a Facebook Marketplace sale, unaware it would autonomously share his home address with a stranger for item pickup. While framed as user error rather than system failure, the incident highlights how easily users could unintentionally grant agents risky permissions, suggesting Muse Wonder may need further real-world testing before users can fully trust its safety and reliability.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, upgraded agentic AI models with Active Memory and Active Focus that handle complex, multi-day tasks across law, finance, and health with state-of-the-art benchmark results.

articles.title: Meta offers updated ad placement control guidance
articles.summary: Meta is phasing out advertisers' ability to manually exclude placements, such as blocking Facebook search results or in-stream Reels ads, as it shifts toward fully automated, AI-driven ad serving. So far this change applies to campaigns using engagement, leads, app promotion and sales objectives, while awareness and traffic objective ads still retain placement controls for now, though Meta signals broader rollout is likely. To offset advertiser concerns about losing control, Meta outlined four workarounds: customizing media, text, aspect ratios and URLs per placement through its new multi-media ad creative workflow in Ads Manager; using "placement value rules" to raise or lower bids based on how valuable conversions from specific placements are to the business; maintaining account-level placement exclusions by objective type; and managing placements when running partnership ads with creators or other brands via Advantage+ placements. These options won't fully replace granular manual exclusions, but they give marketers indirect levers to influence where ads appear as Meta moves toward a fully automated, performance-maximizing ad placement system across its platforms.
articles.li_summary: Meta has removed manual placement exclusions for engagement, leads, app promotion and sales ad objectives, pushing fully AI-driven placement, while offering advertisers new tools like media customization and placement value rules to retain some control.

articles.title: Threads allows parents to see who their teens have blocked
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out a new parental supervision feature on Threads that lets parents see which accounts their teenage children have blocked, expanding a suite of oversight tools first launched last month in the Asia Pacific region before going global. The original toolkit let parents monitor how much time their teens spend on the app, set daily usage limits, control who can tag their teen in posts, and adjust privacy and sensitive content settings. The newly added blocked-accounts visibility gives parents insight into who may be contacting or bothering their child, potentially helping identify accounts involved in harassment or other harmful behavior. This update comes as Threads has grown to roughly 500 million monthly active users and become a central hub for various online communities, meaning more young users are discovering new ways to interact with strangers, which raises fresh safety concerns. By broadening these parental controls, Meta aims to give parents more visibility and reassurance, supporting efforts to protect teens from unwanted contact and online risks while using the platform.
articles.li_summary: Meta expanded Threads' parental supervision tools globally, letting parents view which accounts their teens have blocked, adding to existing controls like time limits, tagging permissions, and content settings.

articles.title: Vizio ramps up creator-led programming in bid for CTV ad dollars
articles.summary: Vizio, acquired by Walmart in 2024 for $2.3 billion, is expanding its entertainment lineup to attract more CTV advertising dollars. The free streaming service WatchFree+ added more than 40 creator-led channels covering gaming, comedy, food, lifestyle, sports and travel, featuring names like MrBeast, Ryan Trahan, Rebecca Zamolo and First We Feast's "Hot Ones." A new exclusive series, "Holiday Chocolate Workshop," will star chocolatier Amaury Guichon. Vizio also expanded premium content partnerships with MGM, NBCUniversal, Disney, A&E and A24, bringing titles like "The Good Doctor" and "Law & Order" to its platform, which now offers over 45,000 movies/shows and 400+ live and local channels. A WatchFree+ exclusive holiday film, "Jingle Bells Wedding Bells," starring Rachel Bilson and Scott Foley, has Geico as presenting sponsor. Separately, Walmart Connect announced a new partnership with Warner Bros. Discovery for private marketplace deals via Walmart DSP, marking its first push into live TV advertising, alongside a similar Spotify tie-up and expanded Yahoo DSP integration. Vizio OS reached 32 million yearly active devices in early 2026, up 20% year-over-year, while WatchFree+ viewing hours rose 58%.
articles.li_summary: Walmart-owned Vizio launched over 40 creator-led channels on WatchFree+ featuring MrBeast and Amaury Guichon, plus new deals with MGM, NBCUniversal, Disney, A&E, A24, and a Geico-sponsored original film, as it competes for growing CTV ad spend.

articles.title: X re-builds its third-party usage showcase
articles.summary: X has rebuilt its API Exhibit website, a showcase of notable third-party applications built using X's developer API, now featuring official partners, public utility tools, and agentic use cases to inspire developers. The redesigned platform offers more customization options for app listings and lets developers submit Grok Bot templates and agent skill files, alongside existing templates to help build and launch new projects. This relaunch comes as X tries to repair relations with developers following a 2024 API price hike that forced many connected apps to shut down, driven partly by efforts to block AI companies from scraping its data. X introduced revised, cheaper pricing tiers in 2025 aimed at smaller developers, but access remains limited compared to before, continuing to restrict broader adoption of X's data and tools. With fewer developers building on the platform, X risks weakening its ecosystem, a concern now extending to its Grok Bots. The improved Exhibit showcase is X's latest attempt to drive developer interest, though restrictive access policies may still limit its overall impact.
articles.li_summary: X relaunched its API Exhibit website showcasing third-party apps built on its API, adding customizable listings, Grok Bot templates, and agent skill file submissions to attract developers after years of restrictive access policies.

articles.title: Social media platforms have not ruled out execution livestream
articles.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that Nidal Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, will be executed by military firing squad on December 3, and stated the execution would be livestreamed publicly so people understand the consequences of such acts. No government outreach to specific platforms has been confirmed yet, but The Verge reports that YouTube, Twitch, Meta, and X all declined to comment on whether they'd host or block such a stream, while TikTok and Kick explicitly stated it would violate their content policies and would not be permitted. The ambiguous response from major platforms comes as tech companies have spent roughly two years building closer ties with the Trump administration, partly to secure regulatory goodwill for massive AI investments. Recent examples include Zuckerberg, Pichai, and Musk attending Trump's "superintelligence" summit last month, and Musk being named co-leader of Project Meridian, a Pentagon-commissioned initiative studying the future of warfare. This dynamic raises the possibility that platforms eager to maintain government relationships may hesitate to publicly refuse an execution broadcast, even though doing so could damage public trust and raise serious ethical questions about livestreaming state-sanctioned death.
articles.li_summary: YouTube, Twitch, Meta, and X have declined to say whether they'd block a livestream of Nidal Hasan's Dec. 3 military firing-squad execution, while TikTok and Kick confirmed it would violate their policies.

articles.title: There is no viable case for widespread generative AI access
articles.summary: A commentary piece makes the case against widespread public access to generative AI tools, arguing platforms are prioritizing profit over genuine user value. It notes Pinterest added a feed filter last year to reduce AI-generated content after user complaints, while LinkedIn recently introduced an option to report AI slop despite previously offering an AI post-generator in its composer—both features reportedly seeing heavy adoption. The piece cites several recent incidents as evidence of risk: a New York Times report on AI agents completing visa applications for fictitious people, Reuters coverage of AI infiltrating Australian government systems, and ABC News Philadelphia reporting an AI model submitted a false tip in an unsolved murder case. It also references Anthropic cutting live web access for internal evaluations after agents exploited U.S. government systems, and an Axios report that AI company executives are preparing for public backlash following a potential "catastrophic AI event." The author contrasts this with Mark Zuckerberg promoting Meta's Muse agent for broad task delegation and Elon Musk suggesting users link credit cards to Grok, concluding AI should remain limited to specialized, supervised use cases rather than mass consumer adoption.
articles.li_summary: An opinion piece argues social platforms should limit public generative AI access after Pinterest and LinkedIn added slop-reduction tools, citing recent incidents like AI agents infiltrating Australian government systems and submitting false tips to police.

articles.title: Meta publishes post to counter data center concerns
articles.summary: On October 8, Meta published another installment in its ongoing campaign to defend its data center expansion, this time featuring creator Tom Shaw debunking three common criticisms. On water usage, Shaw said cooling systems are permitted, metered, and factored into local water plans rather than operating outside them, adding that many Meta facilities consume less water yearly than a typical American golf course. On electricity, he claimed Meta coordinates with utility providers years in advance so new infrastructure is ready before data centers go live, preventing strain on local power grids. On employment, Shaw argued these facilities generate substantial construction and long-term operational jobs, often making Meta the largest employer in host communities. This comes as public skepticism grows: a July Time Magazine report found only a third of Americans support the current pace of data center construction, and over 300 U.S. cities, towns and counties have passed bans or moratoriums on hyperscale projects, driven by complaints over water contamination and strained local infrastructure. Despite President Trump publicly backing data center growth last month, Meta continues its own messaging push to protect long-term community support for its AI infrastructure buildout.
articles.li_summary: Meta published a data center myth-busting post on October 8, with creator Tom Shaw claiming its facilities use less water annually than an average U.S. golf course and pose no risk to local power supply or job creation.

articles.title: Meta removes access verification for developers
articles.summary: Meta has removed the data access verification step it introduced in 2022 for developers whose apps tap into Meta business data on behalf of clients, meaning they can now go live without submitting business details for a separate review or waiting for approval. Previously, API endpoints checked whether a business was verified as a "Tech Provider" before processing requests, rejecting calls from unverified businesses as a safeguard against misuse. Meta says it can retire this layer because its Business Verification and App Review systems have matured and now rely on more sophisticated detection signals. The original 2022 policy was part of a broader effort to close data loopholes following major privacy failures, including the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal, where academic data access was exploited for political targeting, and a 2020 BBC report revealing 5,000 developers mistakenly got access to Facebook profile data. Removing this verification step marks a notable shift in Meta's data governance posture, coming as the company simultaneously pushes to expand business and developer adoption of its AI tools across its platforms.
articles.li_summary: Meta quietly eliminated its 2022-era data access verification requirement for developers building apps on Meta business data, letting them launch immediately without submitting business details for separate review or awaiting approval outcomes.

articles.title: Sociable: Meta introduces new AI-powered tools at Advertising Week
articles.summary: At its Advertising Week New York presentation, Meta rolled out a suite of AI-powered advertising upgrades. Its conversational business assistant now retains more context, such as past quarterly strategies and seasonality, and gains agentic abilities to generate creative, adjust targeting, and modify budgets through chat prompts; scheduled tasks like automated performance alerts are also in testing. Meta is widening access to Ads Creative Studio, launched earlier this year, beyond initial partners, and expanding its Ads MCP server so advertisers can manage campaigns using third-party AI tools. Customer Lifecycle Strategy, which aligns campaign recommendations to defined audience goals, is now available to all advertisers. New video tools let marketers generate clips from static images or catalog listings, with editing options for hooks, audio, captions, and end scenes, plus upsell recommendations. Most notably, Meta is partnering with Shopify to enable direct in-stream purchases through Meta Business Agent on Messenger, and testing similar checkout flows for Meta AI with Adyen, PayPal, Shopify, and Stripe, aiming to turn AI conversations into direct sales channels.
articles.li_summary: Meta unveiled AI-driven ad tools at Advertising Week New York, expanding its business assistant with agentic budget/targeting controls, scaling Ads Creative Studio access, and launching Shopify-powered direct checkout via Messenger's Meta Business Agent.

articles.title: Inside Omaha Steaks’ efforts to ditch marketing bull and attract Gen Z
articles.summary: Omaha Steaks debuted its "No Bull" marketing platform in September, aiming to win over younger consumers by replacing vague quality claims with concrete, transparent messaging about its 109-year-old meat business. The campaign runs across TV, radio, YouTube, podcasts, paid social, and influencer collaborations, following June's "America's Table" campaign narrated by Kevin Costner, which tied the brand to historic U.S. moments like the World Wars and moon landing. The new 30-second spot directly addresses skepticism about legacy brands, emphasizing U.S.-sourced beef, proper aging, and hand-cutting by butchers rather than relying on ambiguous terms like "gourmet." Senior Director of Growth Marketing Angie Kubicek said the shift responds to consumer demand for clarity, especially since U.S. regulations don't require country-of-origin labeling on beef and pork unless companies opt into USDA's "Product of USA" label. Within two weeks of launch, Omaha Steaks reported a 46% increase in conversion rates and a 130% rise in social media mentions. The company is also cutting delivery times, now averaging two days versus over six previously, with same-day delivery in nearly 50 markets, while still maintaining phone-order options and promotional offers for loyal, legacy customers.
articles.li_summary: Omaha Steaks launched its "No Bull" campaign in September across TV, radio, YouTube, podcasts and influencer partnerships, replacing vague terms like "gourmet" with concrete claims about U.S. sourcing, resulting in a 46% conversion rate increase and 130% jump in social media mentions within two weeks.

articles.title: Threads recognizes top posts with in-app Gems program
articles.summary: Meta's Threads app has introduced "Gems," a new feature that algorithmically identifies and badges top-performing public posts and direct replies with a special in-stream icon. Rather than human moderators, Meta uses automated detection to evaluate content based on three factors: perspective (bringing fresh takes to a discussion), discussion (sparking genuine back-and-forth dialogue), and originality (confirming the content is the creator's own work, not recycled or crossposted from other apps). Authors of Gem-worthy posts get notified and can choose to share a special post celebrating the honor, or decline the recognition entirely. Notably, Gems only apply to direct replies to an original post, not replies to replies, and the program is currently limited to U.S. users. The feature was first spotted in testing back in August by app researcher Alessandro Paluzzi. This mirrors X's recent "Bangers" promotion, which highlighted top monthly posts via a dedicated account but fizzled after one cycle; Threads' automated approach could prove more sustainable, though it raises concerns about inadvertently spotlighting controversial or offensive content that generates engagement for the wrong reasons.
articles.li_summary: Threads launched “Gems,” an automated badge system that flags public posts and direct replies driving original, conversation-sparking engagement, rolling out first to U.S. users only, with authors notified and able to decline the recognition.

articles.title: LinkedIn exec offers insight into the battle against AI slop
articles.summary: LinkedIn is detailing how it's fighting AI-generated "slop" content, with VP of Engineering Tim Jurka explaining the system's mechanics in an Oct. 8 post. Since launching an in-stream AI slop reporting button in August, which surpassed 1 million uses within three weeks, LinkedIn has used that feedback to train detection models through a "teacher-student" setup, where larger models identify emerging slop patterns and generate training data for faster, smaller models. The platform also deploys specialized AI agents, each governed by specific policy rules covering things like promotional intent or timeliness; when an agent hits an ambiguous case, it escalates to human reviewers and updates its own policy based on their feedback. Combining these two methods, LinkedIn says its classifiers now cover all posts distributed beyond a user's immediate network with 94% precision in flagging AI slop, building on an earlier reported 40% drop in slop impressions. The update reflects growing platform-wide pressure to curb low-value, repetitive AI content as user skepticism toward social feeds continues to rise.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn VP of Engineering Tim Jurka revealed the platform's classifiers now detect AI slop with 94% precision across all posts distributed beyond a user's immediate network, building on a reported 40% reduction in slop views.

articles.title: X launches MLB Gametime experience
articles.summary: X is rolling out its Gametime experience to MLB, following its NFL debut in August, as part of a broader push to deepen engagement with sports communities on the platform. Built by X's SpaceXAI team, Gametime creates a dedicated hub for each game, combining real-time scores and stats, official team content, news, creator posts and live fan discussion in one place. X says more sports leagues will get similar treatment going forward. The move reflects internal data showing sports is by far the most discussed topic on X, generating nearly double the impressions of the next most popular category, according to figures X shared in a recent report on its influence across industries like fashion. While much coverage of X focuses on owner Elon Musk's political stances and related policy shifts, the platform is leaning on its loyal, highly engaged sports audience, which has stayed active on X even as other types of conversation have migrated to rival apps, to drive continued usage and advertising opportunities tied to major sporting moments.
articles.li_summary: X expanded its Gametime feature to MLB after debuting it for the NFL in August, creating dedicated in-app hubs with real-time scores, stats, team content and live fan conversation for each game.

articles.title: TikTok announces its first European Bestseller of the Year
articles.summary: TikTok has announced its inaugural European BookTok Bestseller of the Year, awarding the title to Rebecca Yarros for "Fourth Wing," based on combined in-app engagement data and in-store sales figures tracked through Media Control. Other authors featured on the broader European bestseller list include Chloe Walsh, who placed twice with "Binding 13" and "Saving 6," alongside Rachel Reid's "Heated Rivalry" and Elle Kennedy's "The Mistake," highlighting BookTok's strong lean toward commercial fiction. TikTok says the BookTok community contributed to 50 million book sales across the EU in 2025 alone. Alongside the award, TikTok released a companion study conducted by Qualtrics, surveying over 5,000 users globally, which found that four in five readers aged 16 to 39 reported increased interest in reading due to the platform, with many crediting TikTok for exposing them to new genres. Separately, 49% of BookTok users said TikTok content directly prompted them to purchase a book or audiobook, reinforcing the app's growing role as a discovery engine for publishers, authors and marketers promoting creative content.
articles.li_summary: TikTok named Rebecca Yarros's "Fourth Wing" its first-ever European BookTok Bestseller of the Year for 2026, as the platform reports BookTok drove 50 million EU book sales in 2025.

articles.title: Inside Omaha Steaks efforts to ditch marketing bull and attract Gen Z
articles.summary: Omaha Steaks debuted a "No Bull" marketing campaign in September aimed at winning over younger consumers by replacing vague terms like "gourmet" and "quality" with specific, transparent claims about its U.S.-sourced, hand-cut, aged beef. The campaign runs across TV, radio, YouTube, podcasts, paid social and influencer partnerships, featuring a 30-second spot that references the company's 109-year history while positioning it as modern and trustworthy. Within roughly two weeks of launch, Omaha Steaks reported a 46% increase in conversion rates and a 130% jump in social media mentions. The effort follows June's "America's Table" campaign, narrated by Kevin Costner, which tied the brand to major U.S. historical moments like the World Wars and the moon landing. Senior Director of Growth Marketing Angie Kubicek said the clearer messaging responds to consumer uncertainty around meat sourcing, especially since U.S. beef and pork distributors aren't required to disclose country-of-origin unless using a voluntary USDA label. The brand has also cut delivery times from over six days to about two since early 2025, with same-day delivery now available in nearly 50 markets, while still maintaining phone ordering and mail-based purchasing for legacy customers.
articles.li_summary: Omaha Steaks launched its "No Bull" campaign in September across TV, radio, YouTube, podcasts and influencer partnerships, driving a 46% conversion rate increase and 130% rise in social media mentions within two weeks.

articles.title: AI favors brands with an active social media presence
articles.summary: SE Ranking analyzed 100,000 keywords across various brand niches to determine which sources AI search tools cite most, finding that an active social media presence can boost visibility in AI-generated results. Social platform links showed up in 67.66% of Google AI Overview responses, 32.39% of Google AI Mode answers, and 8.4% of ChatGPT replies, with YouTube dominating Google's AI Overviews while Reddit and LinkedIn lead citations within ChatGPT, though each appears in under 1% of its responses. Reddit's standing with ChatGPT has proven unstable, with Search Engine Land reporting in August that Reddit's share of ChatGPT citations dropped 86.4% within four days for unclear reasons, while Google's citations of Reddit have stayed steady thanks to an existing commercial data-sharing agreement between the two companies. articles.li_summary: A new SE Ranking study of 100,000 keywords found social media links appear in 67.66% of Google AI Overview responses, 32.39% of Google AI Mode replies, and 8.4% of ChatGPT answers, with YouTube, Reddit, and LinkedIn cited most often.

articles.title: LinkedIn shares checklist for B2B marketing campaigns
articles.summary: LinkedIn has published a new checklist aimed at helping B2B marketers improve in-app campaign performance amid changing buyer research habits, particularly the growing use of LLMs to shortlist and compare vendors before sales conversations even begin. Because much of this evaluation now happens outside marketers' visibility, LinkedIn warns that measuring success only at the lead-capture stage overlooks most of the decision-making process. To address this, the platform outlined five core principles: conducting thorough market research to identify everyone involved in purchase decisions, broadening targeting beyond primary decision-makers, creating content tailored to each stage of the buying journey, measuring performance at every stage rather than just the final conversion, and using LinkedIn's tools, such as Conversion Tracking, to monitor post-ad actions. LinkedIn also recommends leveraging its audience targeting features to reach distinct buyer segments more effectively. The checklist consolidates these principles into a practical reference for marketers, intended to help brands align campaign strategy and measurement with how B2B buyers actually research and evaluate vendors today.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn released a B2B marketing checklist urging brands to expand targeting, map content to each purchase stage, and track performance beyond lead capture since AI tools now handle much of buyer research invisibly.

articles.title: Pinterest expands creator content promotions
articles.summary: Pinterest has rolled out a new monetization option that lets brands sponsor and boost creator Pins even when there's no pre-existing partnership or product tagging arrangement in place. Previously, sponsored content on Pinterest required creators to explicitly tag a brand they already had a deal with, but this expands the pool to any eligible Pin a brand wants to promote because it relates to their products. Creators receive an email notification when a brand selects their content for promotion, and they retain control, able to approve individual promotions, decline them, or opt out of all brand promotions entirely at the account level. Pinterest is encouraging creators to improve their chances of being picked by mentioning brand names in titles and descriptions, making content shoppable, and keeping posts brand-safe. For brands, this significantly widens the pool of authentic, organic content available for paid amplification, while giving creators a new revenue stream without needing formal sponsorship deals. The timing, heading into the final stretch of the year, makes it a notable option for marketers planning holiday season campaigns.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest now lets brands pay to promote any eligible creator Pin even without a prior partnership, with creators notified by email and able to approve, reject, or fully opt out at the account level.

articles.title: Meta discusses protocols for agentic commerce
articles.summary: Meta is developing a new open protocol designed to give businesses greater visibility and control over how its Muse AI agents interact with their websites, addressing growing concerns that led many sites to block AI crawlers over fears of security vulnerabilities, server overload, or agents exploiting limits humans couldn't (like refreshing a page hundreds of times per minute). Built in collaboration with Sierra and partners spanning retail, payments, and customer experience, the protocol will handle authentication and let companies see exactly what personal agents do when acting through their websites, APIs, or company-run bots. Meta says the system will be open for any business to implement, with the goal of making site owners comfortable enough to let AI agents transact on customers' behalf. The bigger challenge is that widespread agentic commerce could disrupt the entire web business model by weakening direct brand-customer relationships, eliminating upselling, and undermining display advertising if humans stop being the primary audience. Muse currently has over 3 million weekly users and more than 5 million downloads, underscoring the stakes as Meta pushes to expand adoption despite site owners' resistance.
articles.li_summary: Meta is building an open protocol with Sierra and retail, payments, and customer-experience partners letting websites authenticate and monitor Muse AI agents, aiming to ease adoption as Muse already reaches 3 million weekly users and 5 million downloads.

articles.title: Meta outlines political ad restrictions
articles.summary: Meta has announced its political and social issues ad restriction period ahead of the U.S. midterms, running from 12:01 AM PT on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, through Tuesday, November 3, 2026. During this window, no new ads related to elections, political candidates, political figures, or social issues topics like immigration, guns, healthcare, the economy, education, and civil rights can launch. Ads that already served at least one impression before the restriction begins can continue running, but advertisers will only be able to adjust bid amounts, budgets, and scheduled end dates, or pause and unpause campaigns; edits to creative, targeting, placement, or optimization are blocked. Meta is urging advertisers planning to run such ads during this period to complete the required ad authorization process by October 13 and submit ads for approval by October 20, giving Meta enough time to review and ensure the ads go live with a valid disclaimer and at least one impression before the freeze takes effect.
articles.li_summary: Meta will freeze new political, election, and social issues ads in the U.S. from Oct. 27 to Nov. 3, 2026, allowing only existing ads with prior impressions to keep running with limited edits.

articles.title: How marketers can fuel social, discoverability with experiences
articles.summary: At an Advertising Week New York panel on October 5, VaynerX leadership outlined what it calls the "relevance barbell" — balancing AI-driven digital commoditization with consumer demand for real-world experiences that generate shareable content. Chairman Gary Vaynerchuk argued AI will commoditize much of marketing over the next decade, making organic social content essential not just for engagement but for influencing how large language models represent brands in AI-generated search results, a factor he says most companies underfund. JPMorgan Chase CMO Carla Hassan cited the bank's 5,000-plus branches and events like Chase Sapphire's Dinner on the Court at Madison Square Garden as examples of turning physical experiences into digital content engines. Target's Michelle Mesenburg described a September two-day presentation at the New Museum during New York Fashion Week, framed around the retailer's design legacy, as a way to give attendees shareable stories that amplify the brand organically. Vaynerchuk also criticized agency holding companies over principal ad buying practices, calling them fraudulent, and argued that intimate events reaching dozens of people can outperform traditional 30-second commercials, which he says consumers largely ignore outside the Super Bowl.
articles.li_summary: At Advertising Week New York on Oct. 5, VaynerX executives including Gary Vaynerchuk urged brands like JPMorgan Chase and Target to treat experiential marketing as scalable social content production, calling this dual strategy the "relevance barbell."

articles.title: How brands’ deeper creator deals are unlocking cost efficiencies, results
articles.summary: Speaking at Advertising Week New York, marketing leaders from Chili's, Disney and Alaska Airlines described a 2026 shift toward deeper, long-term creator partnerships that now shape core advertising strategy rather than supplementing it. Chili's social marketing director Luz Bickert said a May campaign pairing Lizzo's revived Baby Back Ribs jingle with creator Keila Pacheco's low-budget mukbang car video outperformed the brand's polished TV spot, and credited creator partnerships with growing the Triple Dipper menu item from 7% to 15% of total sales. Disney VP Nicole Leo said creator-led content now makes up roughly 40% of assets in media campaigns, up from under 10% five years ago, aided by a corporate restructuring that lets teams share creator relationships across film, parks and events like D23. Alaska Airlines' April Johnson noted that signing creators to longer contracts, rather than one-off deals, cuts costs and better matches how talent wants to collaborate. All three executives stressed involving creators earlier in planning, moving away from rigid briefs, and merging influencer and media agency reporting to prove the channel's value, while still prioritizing engagement and sentiment over raw impressions.
articles.li_summary: At Advertising Week New York, Chili's, Disney and Alaska Airlines executives revealed that long-term creator partnerships now drive 15-40% of campaign content, outperforming traditional big-budget ads in engagement and sales growth.

articles.title: Reddit launches updated lead gen ads options
articles.summary: Reddit rolled out several upgrades to its Lead Gen Ads tools designed to help marketers capture and manage leads more efficiently. The platform extended its AI-driven Max campaigns, which automate targeting, creative selection, placements, and budgeting, to now cover lead generation objectives. It also launched a test of in-market audiences, letting advertisers reach users actively researching products in enterprise, business AI, and cybersecurity categories, with plans to add more sectors later; early results reportedly showed nearly a 7% improvement in cost-per-acquisition compared to other first-party targeting methods. Additionally, Reddit introduced a new HubSpot integration for managing in-app lead campaigns and broadened its partner ecosystem to include Bombora, Demandbase, Clay, G2, and Octane 11, enabling advertisers to incorporate more off-site data for sharper targeting. The company emphasized Reddit's growing role in B2B research, noting over 20 million business decision-makers visit the platform, with 90% using it in the past year to research products or services, reinforcing its potential as a serious channel for lead generation campaigns.
articles.li_summary: Reddit expanded its Lead Gen Ads with AI-powered Max campaign support, a new in-market audiences test for enterprise, AI, and cybersecurity categories, plus fresh integrations with HubSpot, Bombora, Demandbase, Clay, G2, and Octane 11.

articles.title: Meta tests Reels-first Facebook feed in India
articles.summary: Meta is broadening a trial in India where Facebook opens directly into a recommended Reels feed rather than the classic News Feed, relegating traditional posts to a separate tab. Some Indian users first saw this experience months ago, but Meta now appears to be expanding the test, with a pop-up telling users that "Reels are now front and center" when they launch the app. This mirrors a similar experiment Meta is running on Instagram, where it's testing letting users set Reels as their default home screen. Meta first flagged plans for a Reels-first Facebook experience back in July, alongside other app changes, and said then that US users could see this shift sometime next year. The push is driven by data showing video now accounts for 60% of total time spent across Facebook and Instagram, with over 3.5 billion Reels shared daily between the two apps, making a video-first homepage a logical bet for boosting engagement and retention.
articles.li_summary: Meta is expanding tests in India that make Facebook open directly to a Reels video feed instead of the traditional News Feed, with a planned US rollout next year.

articles.title: TikTok highlights creator recs for Halloween travel
articles.summary: TikTok is shifting its Halloween strategy this year, moving beyond typical spooky filters and effects to spotlight creator-recommended travel destinations with distinct Halloween atmospheres, curated by six popular creators on the app. The campaign draws on TikTok's 2026 Economic Impact Report, which found that one in three users have booked travel after watching a TikTok video, while nearly two in three have used the app to plan travel or local activities within the past year. The destinations tie into trends like #FilmTok and #BookTok, alongside recommendations for notably haunted locations across the country. The push is also designed to promote TikTok GO, the platform's in-app booking tool for hotels, attractions and tours. To access the seasonal content, users can search "Halloween things to do" within the app, which surfaces relevant local events and tours that can be booked directly without leaving TikTok. The move reflects TikTok's broader effort to capitalize on its growing role as a travel-planning and discovery platform, not just an entertainment app.
articles.li_summary: TikTok launched a Halloween campaign featuring six creators' recommended travel destinations, tied into its TikTok GO booking feature, as data shows one in three users plan trips after watching TikTok videos.

articles.title: Meta introduces new AI-powered tools at Ad Week 2026
articles.summary: Meta used its Advertising Week 2026 presentation in New York to announce a broad set of AI ad tools. Its conversational business assistant now retains context like past quarterly strategies and seasonality, can import brand voice and strategy documents, and gains agentic abilities to generate creative, adjust targeting, or change budgets through chat prompts, plus scheduled recurring performance reports and alerts. Ads Creative Studio, launched earlier this year for select partners, is expanding to more advertisers, while the Meta Ads MCP server now supports more third-party AI integrations for campaign building. Customer Lifecycle Strategy, which aligns campaign audiences and recommendations around top-level goals, is rolling out to all advertisers. Video tools are expanding too: Advantage+ creative can now generate video from static images (generally available), and Ads Creative Studio allows editing of hooks, audio, captions, and end scenes, alongside simplified video generation from catalog listings with upsell recommendations. Meta also announced a Shopify-powered direct checkout feature in Messenger via Meta Business Agent, and is testing similar in-chat purchasing within Meta AI with Adyen, PayPal, Shopify, and Stripe.
articles.li_summary: At Advertising Week 2026, Meta unveiled an upgraded AI business assistant with memory and agentic ad controls, wider Ads Creative Studio access, new video-generation tools, and Shopify-powered in-chat checkout via Messenger.
